title: Sequences of Rigid Transformations Review
description: Review ordered rigid-motion sequences, intermediate images, inverse moves, and congruence conclusions.

questions.questionText: Point P is (2, 3). Apply this sequence: translate by <4, -1>, then reflect across the x-axis. What is P''?
questions.explanation: Apply the first step to get (6, 2), then apply the second step to get (6, -2).

questions.questionText: Point P is (-3, 5). Apply this sequence: reflect across the y-axis, then translate by <2, -4>. What is P''?
questions.explanation: Apply the first step to get (3, 5), then apply the second step to get (5, 1).

questions.questionText: Point P is (4, -2). Apply this sequence: rotate 180 degrees about the origin, then translate by <1, 3>. What is P''?
questions.explanation: Apply the first step to get (-4, 2), then apply the second step to get (-3, 5).

questions.questionText: Point P is (-5, -1). Apply this sequence: translate by <3, 6>, then reflect across the y-axis. What is P''?
questions.explanation: Apply the first step to get (-2, 5), then apply the second step to get (2, 5).

questions.questionText: Point P is (1, -6). Apply this sequence: reflect across the x-axis, then translate by <-2, 5>. What is P''?
questions.explanation: Apply the first step to get (1, 6), then apply the second step to get (-1, 11).

questions.questionText: Point P is (6, 2). Apply this sequence: rotate 90 degrees counterclockwise about the origin, then translate by <3, 0>. What is P''?
questions.explanation: Apply the first step to get (-2, 6), then apply the second step to get (1, 6).

questions.questionText: Point P is (-2, 4). Apply this sequence: rotate 90 degrees clockwise about the origin, then reflect across the x-axis. What is P''?
questions.explanation: Apply the first step to get (4, 2), then apply the second step to get (4, -2).

questions.questionText: Point P is (3, -5). Apply this sequence: translate by <-4, 2>, then rotate 180 degrees about the origin. What is P''?
questions.explanation: Apply the first step to get (-1, -3), then apply the second step to get (1, 3).

questions.questionText: Which phrase describes P' in a two-step transformation sequence?
options: The image after the first transformation
questions.correctAnswer: The image after the first transformation
questions.explanation: P' is the intermediate image; P'' is the image after the second step.

questions.questionText: Which phrase describes P'' in a two-step transformation sequence?
questions.explanation: Double prime notation marks the image after the second transformation.

questions.questionText: A point is reflected across the x-axis and then reflected across the x-axis again. What is the final point?
questions.explanation: Reflecting across the same line twice undoes the first reflection.

questions.questionText: A triangle is transformed by a translation and a rotation. What must stay the same?
questions.explanation: Translations and rotations are rigid transformations.

questions.questionText: Why should you not switch the order of transformations unless the problem allows it?
questions.explanation: The same transformations in a different order can land in a different place.

questions.questionText: Which sequence uses only rigid transformations?
questions.explanation: Translations, reflections, and rotations are rigid transformations.

questions.questionText: A sequence of rigid transformations maps one triangle exactly onto another. What does this prove?
options: The triangles have different angle measures.
questions.explanation: Rigid transformations preserve size and shape.

questions.questionText: Point P(2, 3) is translated by <1, -5>, then reflected across the x-axis. What is P''?
questions.explanation: P becomes (3, -2), then (3, 2).

questions.questionText: Point P(-4, 1) is reflected across the y-axis, then translated by <-2, 3>. What is P''?
questions.explanation: P becomes (4, 1), then (2, 4).

questions.questionText: Which two-step sequence is equivalent to no net movement?
options: Rotate 90 degrees clockwise, then rotate 180 degrees
Reflect across the x-axis, then reflect across the y-axis
questions.explanation: Opposite translation vectors undo each other.

questions.questionText: A segment is 9 units long. After a sequence of rigid transformations, how long is its image?
options: It depends on the final quadrant.
questions.explanation: Rigid transformations preserve distances.

questions.questionText: Which statement is always true for a sequence of rigid transformations?
options: The final image is always translated only.
The final image is always in Quadrant I.
The final image is congruent to the original figure.
The final image is always facing the same direction.
questions.correctAnswer: The final image is congruent to the original figure.
questions.explanation: A sequence of rigid transformations preserves size and shape.
